Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 16 s. 2023 MAR 15 2023 MLGOO MA. BELLA P. AGULLANA 2nd Floor Municipal Hall Building, Kalawag III Isulan, Sultan Kudarat Dear Ms. Agullana: This pertains to your letter dated 19 January 2023 addressed to Dir. Josephine C. Leysa, which refers to the Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) representatives to the Local Development Council (LDC). Herein are the relevant facts submitted: The Municipality of Isulan belatedly constituted its Municipal Development Council (MDC) due to lack of accredited CSOs within the sixty-day period as provided under DILG MC 2022-083. The MLGOO facilitated the CSO Assembly during which the CSOs selected eleven (11) members as their representatives to MDC. The Mayor issued an Executive Order reducing the CSO representation to only five (5). The composition of the MDC was questioned as the CSO representatives were selected beyond the 60-day period. Now, the queries forwarded are as follows: 1. Is the Sanggunian correct in saying that those CSOs who failed to comply the accreditation as enunciated in Sec. 108 of R.A. No. 7160 are not anymore qualified for representation in the LDC beyond the 60-day period? 2. Whether or not Municipal Mayor may reduce the number of representations of the CSO in the MDC from 11 to 6 only considering that the CSO voted for themselves that there will be 11 CSOs in the MDC? 3. If the answer is in the affirmative, would the act of the Municipal Mayor contravene the provisions under Memorandum Circular No. 2022-083? 4. If the answer is in the affirmative, would the Mayor incur any liability? On the first query, we answer in the negative. The prevalence of right of representation over the 60-day period prescribed under Section 108 of the Local Government Code is upheld. The interpretation is that although said provision prescribed for the "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

organization of local development councils within a 60-day period, failure to comply the same should not be construed to strip Civil Society Organizations of right of representation. Such Will be an absurd interpretation as it turns against the legislative intent behind the law which is to ensure equal participation of the public in planning for the developmental goals of the locality. As for queries 2, 3 and 4, we consolidate our response stressing that the position of this Department has to be more precise on emphasizing the 25% minimum representation of CSOs. Thus, the reduction of the CSOs' representatives should not, in any way, cause said representation to fall below the minimum of 25% required by Section 107 of the Local Government Code. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you.
